inputs.doc: E-047a · Trains a FRESH ~40M MONTH-BLOCK codec on the pentad tensor: one embedding per CALENDAR MONTH instead of one per 5-day bin. The encoder reads a 7x40 GRID of cells (k_max 7, a pentad month being 6 or 7 bins, short months padded) whose token is the channel embedding plus a learned within-block time-offset embedding; the decoder names a cell through its own q_time query embedding; padded and missing cells ride the existing unobserved-cell path. THAT IS THE POINT: rg_* is a MONTHLY product written into ONE pentad bin per month (measured 2026-08-22, n_rg_live 252/3142 = 8.02%, the mid-month stamp, 79.41% of ocean pixels when present), and the per-bin codec's round trip collapses on exactly those bins (FVU 15-18% vs 0.4-0.5% Argo-free) because 40 channels compete for 32 dimensions — a month block fuses the Argo anchor with its pentads into one representation. ctx carries the CONTINUOUS fraction-of-year phase of the block centre, so the labelling is right from birth. THE EMBEDDING AXIS BECOMES MONTHLY (block labels YYYY-MM), so the follow-on roll is day-matched comparable to the monthly archive's +0.939 corridor line while every input is 5-day data · params ~40M (512x12, 4 heads, d_dec 256, d_z 64, patch 1, k_time 7) · stage stage-1 · data family4_na025_pentad_r2 (C 40, T 3142, sha256 37e146384b…) · steps x batch 200,000 x 512 · resume '' (FRESH codec; a block codec shares no weights with a per-bin one). HYPOTHESIS: fusion beats selection — the 20k stage-2 head on this z beats E-045-A2a's 0.0721 (selection of one bin per month). FALSIFIERS: parity means selection suffices; worse means the architecture is wrong (most likely the grid dilutes the anchor); the roll still calendar-locking under longstart: means fusion changed the input, not the failure. NOTE two per-bin evaluations are SKIPPED with reasons in their own artefacts (train.py end-of-run eval, temporal.py chan_t+1); z_t+1 is the headline. Full design: ml/plans/E047_block_codec.md.
